newsitem.title: FRANCE: ONIC drafts cut in 96/97 maize exports to non-EU.
newsitem.headline: ONIC drafts cut in 96/97 maize exports to non-EU.

text.p: The French cereals office ONIC cut its estimate for French maize exports to non-EU countries in 1996/97 to a range of 250,000 to 1.25 million tonnes from a previous target of between 400,000 and 1.4 million tonnes, industry sources said on Thursday.
This would compare with maize exports outside the European Union of 164,000 tonnes in the 1995/96 season.

In a new draft supply/demand report, ONIC slightly raised its forecast for the French 1996 maize crop to 13.66 million tonnes from 13.60 million tonnes forecast last month and 12.4 million tonnes produced in 1995.
The figures were drawn up by an industry panel for official publication on October 9 and remain subject to confirmation.
The draft also suggested that ONIC raise its estimate for the use of maize in animal feed to 2.2 million tonnes from 2.05 million last month and 1.9 million last year.
France would end the 1996/97 season with a maize carryover of 1.99-2.99 million tonnes, slightly above the 1.98-2.98 million tonnes range forecast last month.
This would compare with a carryover stock of 1.65 million tonnes at end-June 1996.
